source_snapshot.test_set: Power Supply - L10 : CRPS -Latch on fault
source_snapshot.procedure: Before Test: verify the SUT configuration against the specification/recipe and clear logs. During Test: offset in bytes from this location to the beginning of the next configuration block. After Test: collect results/photos and check dmesg, syslog, and SEL for unexpected logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Offset in bytes from this location to the beginning of the next configuration block

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Verify the offset-in-bytes field between consecutive configuration blocks using the PSU vendor layout/VPD parser; no vendor tool is supplied in the library.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: The operator reads the PSU configuration-block offset through the vendor tool and compares it with the specification table.

original_test_intent.purpose: Read the CRPS latch-on-fault configuration field that encodes the byte offset from the current configuration block to the next block, then compare the decoded value with the applicable vendor layout.
original_test_intent.target: The identified CRPS PSU configuration-block data and the specific latch-on-fault offset field.
original_test_intent.scope: One applicable CRPS model/firmware instance; no cross-model value is implied.
original_test_intent.operation: A vendor-defined read-only configuration-block decode followed by a specification comparison.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The source states five minutes attended and five minutes machine time; it does not define a loop.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The raw and decoded offset corresponds to the beginning of the next configuration block under the applicable vendor definition.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: CRPS identity and firmware, raw field/block bytes, decoded offset, block boundaries, byte order, decoder/tool version, and the exact applicable specification reference.
ambiguities: The row does not identify the CRPS model, field address, current block, next-block boundary, byte order, expected numeric offset, or approved read command.

deepseek_review_conclusion.agreement: It correctly identifies that a PSU vendor decoder and specification are required.
deepseek_review_conclusion.defect: It describes operator comparison but does not separate missing vendor inputs from automation capability or define safe pre-collection evidence.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 treated the missing field map, byte order, expected offset, read-only tool, and recovery information as a semantic blocker and prohibited guessed PMBus access.

applicable_history.decision: The vendor PMBus Application Note/Firmware Spec and decoder are execution prerequisites; their absence alone is not a permanent BLOCKED condition.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The test purpose and read-only operation are identifiable. Execution depends on model-specific vendor artifacts and parameters, but those dependencies are obtainable prerequisites rather than proof that the testcase is permanently undefined.

available_now: The source identifies the CRPS capability field and the relationship to be checked.
Read-only CRPS/PSU identity, firmware, and BMC inventory evidence may be collected through an already approved management interface.
missing_inputs: Exact CRPS model, slot, firmware/VPD identity, and applicable firmware family
Vendor PMBus Application Note or Firmware Specification
Field address, current and next block boundaries, byte order, encoding, and expected offset
Vendor-approved read-only decoder/tool and exact invocation
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/PSU engineer or PSU vendor supplies and approves the model-specific specification, decoder, parameters, and expected value.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect CRPS FRU/model/slot identity and current firmware through an approved read-only BMC or vendor inventory path.
Preserve existing SEL and management evidence; do not clear logs.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not blind-scan PMBus/SMBus, guess a register, write configuration, reset the PSU, or flash firmware.
Do not claim PASS from identity or inventory data alone.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: An engineer confirms the specification applies to the detected CRPS identity and firmware, supplies a read-only command that returns the defined field, and provides the documented expected offset and decoding rules.

revision_candidate.test_name: CRPS Latch-on-Fault Offset to Next Configuration Block
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that the CRPS latch-on-fault configuration field contains the vendor-defined byte offset from the current configuration block to the next block.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the CRPS model and firmware revision covered by the supplied vendor PMBus configuration-block specification.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The identified CRPS slot and the single vendor-defined offset field; do not apply the expected value to other PSU models or firmware families.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: CRPS identity and slot, firmware/VPD revision, applicable vendor specification, field address, block boundaries, byte order/encoding, expected offset, and approved read-only decoder or command.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Run the vendor-approved read-only configuration-block decode for the identified CRPS and capture the raw field and decoded byte offset. Do not substitute a generic PMBus scan.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Confirm the specification-to-CRPS identity match, management access path, tool compatibility, and non-writing mode. Preserve existing logs.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: CRPS identity/firmware, tool and specification version, raw field bytes, decoded offset, current and next block boundaries, byte order, and timestamped read output.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The expected offset and encoding in the applicable vendor PMBus Application Note or Firmware Specification. The end user performs the final comparison.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only access only. No blind bus scan, configuration write, PSU reset, firmware operation, or log clearing.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: The platform/PSU engineer must approve the specification, detected target, and resolved read-only command before access.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The engineer supplies proprietary artifacts and confirms applicability; the agent may collect the approved readback and evidence.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If the management path becomes unavailable, stop, preserve error/SEL evidence, and follow the approved BMC/PSU access recovery procedure without writing or resetting the PSU.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Stop if the CRPS identity, specification applicability, field map, expected value, read-only property, or management target cannot be confirmed.

identified_defects: V2 conflates missing vendor artifacts and expected parameters with an irreducible semantic blocker even though the field relationship and required read-only operation are identifiable.
The source log-clear instruction would remove diagnostic evidence and is not part of the offset validation.
reason_for_change: Apply the locked user boundary that model-specific vendor specifications and decoders are prerequisites when the purpose and operation can be identified.

new_technical_evidence.supports: The exact offset relationship requested by the original row.
The confirmed prerequisite-versus-BLOCKED boundary for this case.

removed_ambiguities: Separates target identity collection from the gated vendor-field decode.
States that inventory collection is not completion or PASS.
Defines who supplies each proprietary input and how applicability is closed.
resolved_blockers: The missing vendor document and decoder no longer create a permanent automation-classification blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains gated until the applicable field map, expected value, and read-only tool are supplied and matched to the detected CRPS.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's prohibition on guessed PMBus access while replacing the permanent BLOCKED label with explicit prerequisite, ownership, safe pre-collection, prohibited-action, and closure criteria. The agent can now collect identity evidence without falsely claiming that the offset was validated.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The validator preserved the CRPS offset purpose, one-block scope, vendor-decoder dependency, read-only boundary, and prohibition on claiming PASS from raw data alone.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The field is the byte offset from the current configuration block to the beginning of the next block.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 required the same vendor field details but elevated their absence to BLOCKED.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Only an approved read-only decode is permitted; blind bus access and any write/reset are prohibited.
